column2: the writer's notes (doubts; where the article disagrees with the entry): for the data check

Desc says published anonymously in German in London in February 1848: consistent with article (late February). Article says Belgian expulsion 4 March. Legacy quotations of modern commentators left out.

Article says Apia founded 1850s and capital since 1959; desc says New Zealand administration from 1914 (article: occupation from August 1914, governed from 1920 as trust territory): worded as article. 'Hurricane' in desc vs 'typhoon' in article: used article's wording; storm not named otherwise.
Article hedges authorship; text keeps hedge. Desc says 150 psalms; article says 150 in Jewish and Western Christian traditions; I say 'Of the 150'. Commentaries list not used.

Article says Doctor Zhivago first published in Italy 1957 (desc same). Desc says he died 'in disgrace'; not repeated. Article's CIA claim and deportation plans left out. Stalin-cloud-dweller anecdote left out (hedged).

Desc says founded in the 1860s and capital of German East Africa in 1891; article gives 1865 or 1866 and German East Africa Company station 1887, no 1891: year omitted. Desc says Dodoma 'designated'; article: move decided 1974, completed 1996. Rankings, stadiums and notable people left out.

Desc lists empires that used the river; article does not discuss the Chaldean or Seleucid empires, so not mentioned. Article's Akkadian dates 2335-2154 BCE. Climate and dam-displacement figures left out; Early Dynastic start 3100 BCE from article.
Article contradicts itself on Prussian annexation (lead 1864, history 1867): worded 'after the Austro-Prussian War of 1866'.

Desc: Sikh Empire from 1799 (Ranjit Singh); article timeline says 1799 too but history text only gives 1767 Bhangi Misl; wording avoids stating the 1799 year, says 'later became capital of the Sikh Kingdom of Lahore'. Article's population figures conflict (over 14 million vs 11,126,285 in 2017): omitted. Nader Shah in desc not in article; not mentioned. Article says Lahore 'capital of Delhi Sultanate' loosely; used 'several states'.
Nechayev catechism authorship disputed in article: left out. Confession to the emperor left out.

Desc: Jianye and Jiankang capital of Eastern Wu; article only names Jiankang (originally Jianye) for the Six Dynasties and says Eastern Wu capital 229-280; fine. Article says Ming 1368-1421; I stated Ming capital until 1421. Article contradicts on Nanjing Massacre? no.
Desc says first bishopric 968; article gives bishop in 970 (Thietmar), no bishopric date: omitted. Pogrom and population figures left out.
Article's History section is empty; history drawn from lead and Sights. Desc says Parliament created 1554; article only 'early sixteenth century'.
Desc mentions 'benevolent assimilation' and the Philippine-American War by name; the article excerpt does not, so only 'pro-independence rebellion' used.
Article gives 738 BC for King Ping's move to Luoyang; left out (not in desc but a likely slip, 770 BCE usual). Rankings omitted.
Article's Bonpland abduction and Russia 1811/1818 oddity left out.

Article's sentences on terrorist attacks, drug trafficking, mind control etc. left out as sweeping claims; budget figures and 2013 priorities left out (as-of/indices). Desc says Iran coup overthrew Mosaddegh; article lead names the coup only.

Desc says a French and Spanish fleet attacked in 1858 and the Nguyen court ceded it in 1888; article says French troops landed in August 1858 and French rule 1884-1945; no cession year given, so omitted. Rankings, HDI and demographics left out.
Desc's statements on West African pilgrimage routes and rulers are not in the article and were left out. Attendance statistics and COVID restrictions left out.
Desc says 'became the national script in the 20th century'; article says societal acceptance began late 19th century: worded around it. Diaspora and Korean Wave left out.
Article gives death between 183 and 181 BC; desc c. 183 BCE: death year left out.

Article gives founding as 1635; entry says 1636 and names Thomas Hooker. Left the founding date and founders out. Article says Hartford Public High School second oldest; not used. 'first school for deaf children' rephrased from 'oldest school for deaf children'.
Gyroplane No. 1 flight date uncertain in article; left out, entry gives 1907. Cornu not in article; not mentioned.

Article gives Safavid era 1501-1736 and the move to Isfahan in 1598; entry mentions Afghan capture 1722, not in supplied article, so not used. Left out nuclear, surveillance, water, air quality and similar present-day items.
Article gives 1631 dead as 25,000 non-combatants in lead and about 20,000 in History; left the figure out. Archbishopric year 968 omitted (entry has it). Left out events after 2010.
Article also gives Zacharias Janssen's 1590 claim (made by his son); left out because entry dates the earliest compound microscopes c. 1620.
Entry's 868, Liberal Revolution 1820 and 1832-33 siege are not in the supplied article; left out. Left out current mayor, tourism figures and rankings.

Article gives migration date around 1000 CE in lead and 'around 500 CE' in one section, and arrival in Europe 13th-14th century vs 12th century (and as early as 7th); left the 500 CE and 13th century dates out. WWII section is empty in the supplied text, so nothing on genocide added (the entry covers it).
SKIPPED: the article is about the city of São Tomé (capital), the entry describes the island; a text from it would be about a different subject
Article's supplied text does not mention Drebbel 1620 or Bushnell's Turtle; not used. Entry's dates not contradicted.
Entry says Jordan's Arab Legion held it in 1948; not in the article, left out. Left out legal rulings, settlements, population, politics and later developments as present-day matters.
Kept to the supplied text only. The Prelude's posthumous publication by his wife is in the entry and not repeated.
Article says modern city founded by Akbar 1558 and also that Lodi re-established the ancient city 1504-1505; left out Akbar 1558. Left out pollution, politics, visits of leaders.
Entry's Achaemenid and Oghuz statements are not in the article; not used. Omitted health statistics and 2010s remarks.
Article gives deaths as 136 to more than 200 in lead and at least 140 confirmed in body; used 140. Escapes 'over 5,000' in lead vs 'around 5,000'; used 'about 5,000'.

Article says tallest building since 'complete inauguration in 2011', entry says since opening on 4 January 2010; I did not say when it became the tallest building. Total height 829.8 m vs 828 m roof: different measures.

Entry says PLA took Hainan from the Nationalists in 1950; article only says it became an administrative region office on 1 May 1950, so I used that. Left out free trade port plans, politics, environment rankings and South China Sea claims.
Entry says 'among the most prosperous in India' and mentions Kurukshetra and Panipat; the supplied article text does not support these, so left out. Left out economy rankings and pollution.
Article's closing chapters (death, WWI) not in supplied text beyond the death date from the lead.
Article calls 1948 province an integration of 30 princely states plus four Punjab southern hill states; entry says union of some thirty princely states; consistent. Left out rankings and surveys.
Entry says he proclaimed 'total war' in 1943; the article says he pressed Hitler in 1943 and was appointed plenipotentiary 23 July 1944. Text follows the article's wording.

Article says Lausanne was a Celtic and Roman settlement, cathedral built 12th century; entry says consecrated 1275 and bishopric from about 600: cathedral date and bishopric left out of text. Article gives no bishopric facts. 'Population as of' figures omitted.
Entry's 1984 law not in article. Speaker numbers inconsistent in article (400,000 worldwide; max 285,000 native): only 400,000 used. UNESCO endangerment (2019) and language-use debates omitted.
Article says capital since 1757 (same as entry). British conquest 1797 and federation dates not in article. Current mayor, politics omitted.
Entry's Ethiopian Menelik claim not in article. Dates hedged as 'conventional'.
Article says Ur III was 'erroneously called a Sumerian renaissance'; entry says accounts describe a revival: point omitted. Article's writing date inconsistent (c. 3500 BCE vs c. 3350): omitted.

Entry says Suva replaced Levuka in 1882; article says the capital was moved in 1877 and the transfer made official in 1882. Dates of the move left out of text; both versions recorded here. Article 2009 municipal dismissal etc. omitted as recent politics. Article says South Pacific Games in 2003 'third time in 40-year history'; Pacific Games years 1963, 1979, 2003 used (article order slightly muddled).
Article gives death 4 April; entry says a month after inauguration: exact date left out. Rankings omitted.
Article lead says founded 8th century BC, body c. 729 BCE (same as entry). Article lead says destroyed by earthquake in 1169: not used. Entry says rebuilt in Baroque after 1669 and 1693: consistent.
Entry says separation 'in the Middle Ages' (article 1054): consistent. Entry's Ethiopian/Aksumite remark not in article. Omitted: 2018 Constantinople-Moscow schism, adherent numbers, polls.
Article's remarks on approval ratings and 'peacemaker' omitted as judgments. Afghanistan not in the given excerpt.
Entry says Congress Poland promoted cloth-making from 1820s: consistent. Population figures (639,890 as of 2025; 672,185 in 2020) not given. Article's 1823/1828 dates dropped.
Entry says bought from the Lenape in 1626 by Minuit; article has no purchase: left out. Article gives trading post 1624, New Amsterdam named 1626. 9/11, rankings, GDP omitted.

Entry says Greeks founded Zancle; article lead says Sicels founded it in 757 BC, body says Greek colonists in the 8th century: founders left out. Entry says rebelled 1674, article only dates the sack to 1678: revolt year left out. Mamertines and Normans 1061 not in article.

Entry dates c. 1490-1588; article: death 17 July 1588 but tomb epitaph AH 996 (1587-88); death year left out. Birth year disputed in article, not printed. Article contradicts itself on number of buildings: stated as a range. 1935 skull exhumation omitted.
Article contradicts itself on the date of conversion to a church (lead: final decade of 6th century; body: final decades of the fifth century): date left out. Entry's Latin cathedral not in article.
Entry says renamed after Prince Edward in 1799; article says 1798. Renaming year left out. Present-day politics, abortion history omitted.

Article gives imprisonment 1964-1974 but sentence 21 months: left vague as 'eight years in Salisbury' per article text. Entry's 'military takeover' vs article 'coup d'etat': 'army placed under house arrest'. Quoted judgments (dictator, genocide) omitted.
Ramakrishna Mission year not in article, not printed. Entry's Limbdi not in article.
Entry and article consistent on dates. Article says tsar agreed to protectorate 1912 and Uryankhay Krai 1914: only 1914 used. 1990 violence omitted; officeholders and elections omitted.
Entry says Russian expansion under Ivan IV, Yermak from 1581: article says Yermak crossed around 1581 and does not link Ivan IV; consistent.
Article gives Dian conquest as late 2nd century BC in lead and 109 BC in section; consistent. Omitted Nanzhao's Tang title, population as-of date, development ranking.

Article says Shang capital c. 1600-1046 BC and the entry says 1600 to 1400 BCE: only 'around 1600 BCE' printed. Article gives the prefecture seat as 587 CE (lead) and 583 AD (etymology): date left out. Left out the 2021 flood, GDP and rankings.
Article gives construction as 1113-1150 (lead) and commenced 1122, completed 1150 (section); the entry says twelfth century: construction dates left out. Death-date of Suryavarman II also left out.
Entry says Rome conquered the Salassi in 25 BCE; article says around 25 BC: consistent. Omitted politics, demographics statistics, immigration.
Article inconsistent on São Miguel's settlement (colonies there after Santa Maria in 1436, but 'first settled 1449'): date left out.
Article gives Byzantine rule as 536/552 to 571/590 and later; dates left out. Left out demographics percentages, as-of statistics and religion survey.
Entry says prime minister 1868 and 1874-1880, peerage 1876: consistent. Article does not mention Empress of India in the given text: not printed.
Entry says he headed the KMT after Sun, Nationalist Government at Nanjing 1928, moved to Taiwan 1949: consistent with article. Left out 1943 Cairo, Indochina, Ryukyus details.

Entry dates c. 100-c. 170; article gives death as c. 165, c. 168, c. 170 or c. 175: no death date printed. Entry mentions Abbasid translation; the given article text says Arabic manuscripts: Abbasid not printed.

Article says Georgia withdrew in 2008 (lead), officially in August 2009 membership ended (Further developments): year left out; the entry says 2009. Left out Moldova's recent withdrawal, election monitoring, social statistics.
Entry says paramount leader from 1978 until the early 1990s; article lead says 1978 to 1989: end date left out.

Entry says 'President 1965 to 1986', martial law 1972: consistent. Article says martial law formally lifted 1981 yet regime 14 years of autocracy; wording kept to the facts. Left out 'allegedly stole $10 billion', current-president son.
Article gives Romola as 1862-1863 (lead) and 1863 (text): no date for Romola printed. Left out Martin Amis and Julian Barnes ranking, Henry James appearance description.
Article gives Iberia's conversion as 319 or 326 and traditionally 324 (Mirian III): no year printed; entry says 4th century. Left out Y-DNA and cuisine.

Article has almost no political history (nothing on Portuguese traders, Hideyoshi, warrior houses that the entry mentions); the History section is limited to names, the Taihō Code and a theory. Left out politics, universities, sports, economic statistics, as-of population.

Article: Russian State capital 1918-1920 vs Provisional All-Russian Government 1918-1919; entry says 1918-1919: end year not printed except Bolsheviks entered in 1919. Article has Western Siberia capital 1822 and Steppes 1882; entry's 'Steppe region' not dated. Left out mayor, post-Soviet politics, military industry details.

Article gives oral composition 8th-5th to 5th-4th c. BCE with later stages to the 3rd century CE; the entry says late 1st millennium BCE: no numeric dating printed. Left out etymology details of Rama, commentaries list.

Article gives elevation as 6,998 ft and 7,199 ft: not printed. Article does not mention the 1680 Pueblo revolt, Diego de Vargas or Pedro de Peralta, which the entry names; not added. Left out affordability measures, GDP, demographics.
Article text given does not state the 1838 freeing by lottery, Kobzar 1840, Orenburg/Orsk, so these were left to the entry. 'Later became a student' is inferred; Nizhny Novgorod stay left out.
Entry says free port 1719, Illyrian Provinces 1809-1813, Free Territory until 1954; article agrees. Left out immigration, mayor lists, epithets and ranking claims.
Article: Kingdom of Italy 1861, annexed 1860; wrote annexed 1860 only. Omitted modern politics, economy figures.

Entry says archbishops seat 1164; article says archbishopric moved to Östra Aros after the old cathedral burned (1274 overtook; Old Uppsala cathedral 'from 1164' and burned c. 1240). I printed only 'when the cathedral burned down' without date. Used 1160 and 1274 as article gives.
Article dates Herod Agrippa I's death as 44 in outline, entry does not give a year; left out Agrippa. Article date 80-90 AD vs entry 'late 1st century' consistent.
Entry mentions Gupta, Afsharid, Maratha: article says nothing; not repeated. Omitted modern oil, fishing, 2026 Iran War and environmental pressure content.
Article gives Maratha rule as 1740, 1741 and 1758 variously (and 1741-1845); I wrote 'in the 1740s' and avoided 1758. Left out GSDP, HDI, poverty, sanitation figures as indices.
Article: Standard Babylonian dated 13th-10th c. (lead) and 1300-1000 BCE (body); consistent.

Article gives 'Egypt's longest-serving ruler since Muhammad Ali' - omitted. Omitted wealth estimates (poorly substantiated), indices, post-2011 politics. Article says 'prime minister 1981-82'; left out.

Article gives Boudica's revolt cause date as AD 59 (Prasutagus's death); I gave no date. Article on Armenia: Tiridates set by Vologeses, later replaced by Tigranes; entry says settlement placed Tiridates - left out the Armenian details. Article's Tacitus vs Suetonius contradictions on fire hedged as 'Suetonius records a belief'.
Abdication date: entry says March 1917 - no day given. Article's Bloody Sunday date 19 Jan [O.S. 6 Jan] 1905: used 'January 1905'. Left out Rasputin detail beyond heir illness.

Entry says laid out by English settlers and capital since 1981; article says laid out after French invasion 1666 and that no law makes it official capital. I printed the French-invasion date and the 'no law' point as the article's own remark; the editor may prefer to drop that sentence. Article gives 1736 plot under 'Prince Klaas'. EDITOR: removed disputed 'no law declares it the official capital' (the entry: capital of independent Antigua and Barbuda since 1981).

Article gives Venetian possession 1690 and restored 1691 (siege). Entry says Ottomans took it 1417: consistent. Omitted 1997 unrest, economy rankings, Kushner resort, landfill. Wrote 'recognised by UNESCO' - article says 'Masterpiece of the Oral and Intangible Heritage'.

Article says France conquered most of Alsace in 1639 and recognised in 1648; entry says 1648-1681. I left 1639 out. Article says returned to France 1919; entry says 1918 - I wrote 'after the First World War'. Omitted April 2026 political bill, GDP.
Omitted 2020 riots, economy, sports. Article does not mention Valois dukes or Champmol; entry states them, not repeated.
Article's lead says 'In 1824 English traders from Cape Colony' (matches entry 1824). Omitted mayors, tourism numbers, GDP shares, football World Cup.
Article's lead says 128.590 million 'as of 2026'; I gave the 2020 census figure. Omitted GDP, rankings, 2025 crater. Entry mentions Southern Han and Canton System; article does not.
Entry mentions La Salle, Mississippi, Veracruz, New Orleans: article has none of the La Salle material; not repeated. Omitted pollution, oil spills figures, and the 2020s name dispute.
Article doesn't give exact dates of 1536 arrival or 1538 expulsion; entry gives them, not repeated. Left out Calvin and Jews section.

Article's birthplace dispute (Vyatskoye vs Voroshilov) given as 'generally agreed' per Lim Jae Cheon. Article gives 1994 as his designation as successor 'as early as 1974' - omitted. Entry mentions 1980 designation: consistent.

Article says Lübeck became 'immediate city' 1260 (lead) and imperial immediacy 1226; also 'joining Hanseatic League in the 15th century' in Population vs cradle in 12th c. I used 1226 and mid-13th-century leadership, omitted 1260 and the 15th-century line. Free city status 'until 1937' agrees.

Article's lead says first used for divination 'since c. 206 BC' and 'adopted for navigation 11th century'; used 2nd century BCE and 1088 as the body gives. Entry says 'used at sea under Song'; article says 'navigation' by 1088 (not 'at sea').
Article lists children as David and Jan (also Janet); left out.
Entry's founding 1368 and fall 1644 agree with the article.

Article does not mention Qing China (entry does); left out. Article says European cultivation began in the 19th century via Spain; omitted as it sits oddly with the entry's Columbian-exchange framing. Production and market figures left out.

Article's lead says the city 'developed from a largely rural village area into a city in 1979' and the SEZ was designated May 1980 (also 'Special Export Zone' April 1979); wording kept to these. Article says 1980 population 30,000. Left out all rankings, GDP, skyscraper counts, corruption cases, 'as of' figures.

Article says the original charter of Albany is 1686, matches entry. Article says Albany 'the oldest city in New York'. Capital since 1797 is in the lead but omitted from sections (entry has it). Left out crime, rankings, current mayor, economy figures.

Entry says Caesar 'seized' Vesontio in 58 BCE and that it became capital of Maxima Sequanorum; the article says only that the city is first recorded in 58 BC and was capital of the Sequani. Neither point printed.
The article says the Benin Bronzes are technically brass; the entry names them as bronzes. Left Benin out of the text.
Article says Tenzing wrote that Hillary stepped onto the summit first; left out as a contested point. Radiant Living, politics and honours list omitted.
Article says he escaped in March 1941 (recaptured) and again on 28 November 1941; text names only the second. Controversies (Urba, wiretaps, Rwanda) omitted.
Entry's dates 129–c. 216 agree with the Arabic-source date favoured by Nutton; the Suda's c. 199 is mentioned as a disputed view, not as fact.
Entry says Chile and Greece 'destabilised governments'; article does not say that, not repeated.
Article gives the Treatise's date as 1843 in one place and 1844 in another (entry: 1844); year left out.
Article gives first settlement 1803 (Risdon Cove) and founding of the city at Sullivans Cove in 1804, matching entry. 'Second-oldest capital after Sydney' is in the article but not repeated.

Entry says the Kaaba was a pre-Islamic shrine 'visited by pilgrims from across western Arabia' and that Muhammad cleared idols after taking Mecca in 630; the article has no 630 clearing of idols and Webb argues it was never a prominent pilgrimage site. Neither printed; positions attributed.
Entry says script closely related to Telugu's: not in article, not printed. Article's claim of a Kannada manuscript at Alexandria is called contested and was left out.
Omitted contested personal claims (Marable) and the Palestine passage.
Article says the Qing made the Beijing variety official in the early 1900s; not printed.

Entry says crusaders made it seat of an archbishop and Frederick II recovered it in 1229; the article has only Tancred and the Principality of Galilee. Entry says largest Arab city in Israel; article is inconsistent (second largest in demographics); not printed.
Article gives 'as of the 2020 census' population; printed as a census year, not as 'as of'. Left out 2024 earthquake, mayoralty, politics, finance.
Entry's list of dynasties and empires is not in the article, not repeated.
Birth date left out: article gives 9 February 1737 (O.S. 29 January 1736); entry says 1737.
Statehood year omitted: entry says 1972; article says 1972 in the lead and 1971 (Act) in the body.

Article's dates for the governorate are inconsistent (1865 split from Orenburg vs 1781 separate governorate): left the 1865 point out. Entry says fortress 1574, consistent. 1918 State Conference not in article.
Omitted politics, municipal finance, tourism statistics.
Two accounts of the court language origin (Lalibela, Yekuno Amlak) both attributed. Eritrea point not in the article.
Article does not mention Otis's 1852 safety elevator, the Colosseum or the 1857 installation, which the entry gives; not repeated.
Abdication date not given in the text supplied; left as 'abdicated'.

Entry dates c. 494 – c. 434 BCE; article gives Aristotle's death at 60 (c. 430 BC) and others up to 109 years; I give ages as attributed, no death date. Entry says he supported democracy: not in article text, not repeated.

Entry says she 'championed the women's suffrage law of 1947'; article says her power was limited and the bill she supported was dropped; used the article's wording. Birth year 1919/1922 conflict reported as the article does. Birthplace left out (Los Toldos in lead, Junín in sections).
Article dates Amar-Sin's sack c. 1975 BC (doubtful): left out.
Entry says the new town was built by the Margrave of Brandenburg-Bayreuth; article names Christian Ernst. 'Sixth state capital' of 1708 omitted as unclear.
Article gives First Secretary from 1941 (lead) and elected March 1943: left out. Entry says atheist state 1967: not in article text supplied.
Entry's Marburg Colloquy 1529 not in article; not repeated.

Entry dates c. 605–632; article gives 605/15 (Sunni 605; Twelver 612 or 615) and age at death 18 or 27: age left out. Entry says Fatimid descent was central to legitimacy; article says only that the claim was challenged.
The entry gives Faraday 1821, Jedlik 1828, Sprague 1886, Ferraris and Tesla; the article text supplied lacks these, so they are neither repeated nor added. Sturgeon 1832 agrees with the entry.
Article says Guangxu's death was likely murder by arsenic but speculative; left out.
SKIPPED: the article is about the Eure department, not the river the entry describes, and holds under 250 words of substance; nothing on the river's course or the Eburovices
Entry says foreign minister 1985 to 1990; article gives 1985–91 with an interruption: I give only the dated resignation and return.
Casualty figure 190,000 counts England and Scotland including the Bishops' Wars and accidents per the article; deaths from disease are given separately there and left out.
Entry says Rome absorbed their cities by the 3rd century BCE; article gives conquest from the late 4th century BCE, citizenship 90 BCE, incorporation by 27 BCE: I give the article's dates only.

Article mentions 480 BC Romans; kept as 480 BCE. Left out Corsica/WWII liberation details and 2026 figures. Population rounded. Article says Napoleon's exile followed 'forced abdication following the Treaty of Fontainebleau'; text says after the Treaty, consistent with desc (1814-1815).

Article treats Elijah's date as 9th century BC; consistent with desc. Death told only as ascension per the Kings account. Left out Lilith, Sandalphon and other folklore, pagan associations, LDS belief.

Desc says Commission grew from High Authority and merged 1967; article agrees. Desc date 1958 left alone. Desc names Luxembourger presidents Thorn, Santer, Juncker; article does not list Thorn; not repeated. Omitted present-day president, current commissioner count and COVID/anti-terror initiatives. Article says Rey Commission had 14 members; omitted.
Article gives no date for formation in 1873 or the abolition of domains; the desc covers that, not repeated. Population and current data left out. Dogo over two thousand years as stated.

Article: empire 3 Jan 1868 to 3 May 1947, consistent with desc (1868-1947). Left out lists of scholars, timeline detail and censorship. Four sections used; Legacy short paragraph is under 40 words? merged check by checker.

Article says destroyed by Goths in 263 and partly by earthquake 614 in lead, but in History section a military conflict 614/615; text follows the History section with 'excavations indicate'. Desc: Aydinids took Ephesus/Ayasoluk 'in the early 14th century'; article says Menteşoğulları took in 1304 then ceded to Aydinid; text follows the article without Aydinid date. Article gives 1304 surrender vs desc 'early 14th century': consistent. Theatre 24,000 (lead) vs 25,000 (section): left out.
Article gives accession 30 January 1867 in lead but 31 January in timeline: left out the day, used year only. Desc dates consistent. Queen: married Ichijō Haruko 11 January 1869; omitted for length.

Left out the myths of Nicaea and Aura (violence against women), Gnostic narrative, Orphic Phanes detail. Desc says Praxiteles statue and Thespiae chief cult centre: article only says fertility cult at Thespiae; not repeated. Desc: 'later the son of Aphrodite' consistent.

Article says Russia took Erzurum 1829 and returned in same year; 1878 returned; 1916 occupied, followed by reversion in 1918 (Brest-Litovsk): text says each time except last (returned in 1829, 1878; for 1916 article says reverted 1918) - slightly loose. Left out population figures, sports events, pipelines, climate. Desc says Byzantines, Arabs, Armenians, Saltukids, Seljuks; consistent.
Desc dates c. 300 BCE agree. Left out Books I-IV detail, apocryphal attributions to Hypsicles etc. Reception text: ostraca of 3rd century BC reported by article.

Desc is about the Kadesh treaty (not in article); not repeated. Lead dates first decipherable sentence to the 28th century BC, section says 28th or 27th century: left out. Article lead says last known inscription 394 and closing of temples 391 (section) vs 5th century temple closures (lead): used 391/394.

Article: Exeter Cathedral founded in the mid 11th century; desc does not conflict. Desc: siege of 1068 by William the Conqueror: not in article, not repeated. Left out population, economy and transport.

Article lead: 649 Argentine, 255 British, 3 islanders killed; desc says about 650 and 255. Consistent. Left out later garrison size, minefields, culture. Article says Operation Rosario landing 2 April; desc same. General Belgrano sinking date: article section says 'two days' before 4 May, i.e. 2 May; the article section text itself does not give the date directly, used 2 May by inference.

Desc says Vienna and Schiele, Kokoschka; article lists them among Austrian painters; not repeated. Article does not locate Schiele in Vienna. Left out lists of artists by country and lists of authors.

Article gives death 24 Sept 2003 but headstone 25 Sept; left to year. Article: PNC member 1977-1991 but also resigned 1993 (desc 1993): PNC dates left out. Left out stone-throwing incident (2000), FBI surveillance, Shahak foreword and long lists of honours. Desc says born under the British Mandate and taught at Columbia 1963-2003; not repeated beyond birth.

Desc: shared Nobel Peace Prize 1993, unbanned ANC and released Mandela Feb 1990, deputy president to 1996: not repeated. Article does not date the release in the sections excerpted. Left out personal life, marriage scandal, political-personality sections.

Desc mentions proposals to federalise Austria-Hungary and Roman provincial autonomy; neither is in the article, so left out. Left out lists of current federations, Syria/Iraq and conflict section, technical terms like Gleichschaltung. Article gives Israelite confederacy c.1200-c.1000 BCE per Joseph Baratta.

Desc says Palm Grove 'planted in the Islamic period'; the article does not say, so not repeated. Desc says Lady of Elche found at La Alcudia; article says found among Iberian culture finds (museum section), consistent. Left out population statistics by locality, transport, airport, climate. Population rounded as 'about 240,000' (article 242,317 in 2024).

Desc: Nicholson and Carlisle 1800, Davy by 1808, Faraday 1834, gallium 1875, fluorine 1886, aluminium 1886; kept consistent. Article says potassium and sodium were 1807 within 1808 timeline entry. Left out research trends (hydrogen, seawater, iron). Article gives lithium via lithium oxide in timeline and lithium chloride in history: left unspecified.

Article gives Castilian kingship 1475-1504 in lead but jure uxoris from 1474 in text; the dates left out. Joint reign with Isabella, 1492 Granada, Columbus and expulsion in desc; briefly repeated for chronology (Granada 1492, Alhambra Decree, Columbus). Left out children list, Germaine's son John, heraldry and film.

Entry says Urquiza overthrew Rosas in 1852; the article gives no such event, only the 1853 meeting, so left out. Article's text on Urquiza's third term and the 1859/1861 battles omitted (dates tangled). Economy figures omitted as rankings.
Article is inconsistent on when the Provisional Government was formed (27 February in the lead, 3 March in the body) and on the abdication date; both left out. Entry gives only 1917.
Entry says height c. 1811; article gives 1812 for 130 departments and 44 million. Article's Prussian/Sixth Coalition details trimmed.
Bach: article gives baptism 23 March 1685 and probable birth 31 March; inconsistent, so no day given. Politics, mayors and sport omitted.
Entry dates 1957-1993; article agrees. Ending 2009 told as the Community's formal abolition.
Desc's 'about 1000' archbishopric and Stephen's birth not in article; not repeated. Charles I crowned 1301 from the notable-people list.

Desc calls it the Roman capital of the Eburovices; article names the Aulerci as the tribe of Mediolanum Aulercorum and the Eburovices as the source of the name; I only said the latter. Article's dates for Caesar's winter left out as doubtful.
Article gives two heights for the Buland Darwaza (46 m and 54 m); left out.
Omitted WWII, Soviet and recent war sections (grim or after 2010) and present-day population politics. Desc says Ottomans 'main base'; article says one of the most important Turkish ports.
Skipped the article's section on persecution of Christians (it notes its own quote of Stark is mistaken). Entry dates 'captured Jerusalem 1099' agree.
